findings.reason: A paired space-time fan and flux-envelope drawing materially clarifies why one Riemann solution combines a single jump with a continuous fan. It makes the separate shock speed 3/4 and continuous fan boundary speed 3 visible, and relates them to the chord and cubic arc. The original three authenticated tiles contain formulas but no figure. The existing rigorous proof remains complete and independent; that does not remove this explanatory need.

diagram_math_checks.data: Physical axes are x horizontally right and t vertically up; t>0. Shock endpoint (1.35,1.8) satisfies x/t=0.75; dashed fan edge endpoint (5.4,1.8) satisfies x/t=3. Interior ray speeds are 1.1, 1.6, 2.1, 2.6, all strictly between 0.75 and 3.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement profile and proof steps 1.1-1.2 give state 1 left of x=3t/4, fan u=-sqrt(x/(3t)) between the two rays, and state -1 beyond x=3t. At the shock the fan trace is -1/2, and at x=3t it is -1; consequently only the first boundary is drawn as a shock. Interior rays satisfy x/t=f′(u)=3u^2 on -1<u<-1/2 by F2 and step 1.2.

diagram_math_checks.data: f:[-1,1] to R is u cubed. A=(-1,-1), B=(-1/2,-1/8), C=(1,1). Blue arc AB is f on [-1,-1/2]; red chord BC has equation 3u/4+1/4 and slope 3/4. The remaining cubic is dashed.
diagram_math_checks.justification: All three points lie on f. Chord slope (1+1/8)/(1+1/2)=3/4 equals f′(-1/2); f′(-1)=3. Step 1.1 factors f(u)-(3u/4+1/4)=(u-1)(u+1/2)^2<=0 on [-1/2,1], so the chord lies above the cubic. On [-1,-1/2], f″=6u<0 and f′ falls from 3 to 3/4. Joining to the chord keeps the derivative nonincreasing, yielding the concave majorant in step 4.1. Any concave majorant is at least the cubic arc and at least the chord between B and C, so this is the stated concave hull.

diagram_math_checks.data: A, B and C are filled closed points; the hull includes all three. Finite space-time rays are schematic truncations from their common initial origin and carry no open/closed function-value claims at the shock.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The hull is defined on the closed interval [-1,1], and both joins meet exactly at B. The source does not select a value on the shock ray; no point-value convention is introduced. These are open fan rays/curve segments rather than a named-node graph, so graph-cycle closure is inapplicable. The actual rendered cubic arc and chord meet visibly at B and the dashed cubic meets C.
